title: Second-highest salary
prompt: Return the second-highest distinct salary as a single value.
solution: SELECT MAX(salary) FROM employees WHERE salary < (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM employees)

title: Headcount per department
prompt: List every department with its number of employees, including departments with none. Sort by headcount, highest first, then by department name.
solution: SELECT d.name, COUNT(e.id) AS headcount FROM departments d LEFT JOIN employees e ON e.department_id = d.id GROUP BY d.id ORDER BY headcount DESC, d.name

title: Employees on no project
prompt: List the names of employees who aren't assigned to any project.
solution: SELECT e.name FROM employees e LEFT JOIN assignments a ON a.employee_id = e.id WHERE a.employee_id IS NULL

title: Earning more than their manager
prompt: List the names of employees who earn more than their manager.
solution: SELECT e.name FROM employees e JOIN employees m ON m.id = e.manager_id WHERE e.salary > m.salary

title: Top earner in each department
prompt: For each department, return the department name, the employee name and salary of its highest-paid employee. Include everyone tied for first.
solution: SELECT d.name, e.name, e.salary FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON d.id = e.department_id WHERE e.salary = (SELECT MAX(x.salary) FROM employees x WHERE x.department_id = e.department_id)

title: Well-paid departments
prompt: Return department name and average salary, rounded to whole dollars, for departments whose average is above 120,000. Highest average first.
solution: SELECT d.name, ROUND(AVG(e.salary)) AS avg_salary FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON d.id = e.department_id GROUP BY d.id HAVING AVG(e.salary) > 120000 ORDER BY avg_salary DESC

title: Top two salaries per department
prompt: Return department name, employee name and salary for the two highest salary levels in each department. Employees with equal salaries share a place, so a department can return more than two people.
solution: SELECT department, name, salary FROM (SELECT d.name AS department, e.name, e.salary, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY e.department_id ORDER BY e.salary DESC) AS r FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON d.id = e.department_id) WHERE r <= 2

title: Running payroll by hire date
prompt: List each employee's name, hire date and the running total of salaries of everyone hired up to and including them. Order by hire date.
solution: SELECT name, hired_on, SUM(salary) OVER (ORDER BY hired_on) AS running_total FROM employees ORDER BY hired_on

title: Customers who never ordered
prompt: List the names of customers who have never placed an order.
solution: SELECT c.name FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE o.id IS NULL

title: Products nobody ordered
prompt: List the names of products that don't appear in any order.
solution: SELECT name FROM products WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT product_id FROM order_items)

title: Orders per month
prompt: Count orders of any status per month. Return the month as YYYY-MM and the count, in month order.
solution: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', ordered_on) AS month, COUNT(*) FROM orders GROUP BY month ORDER BY month

title: Repeat customers
prompt: Return the name and order count of customers with at least two orders of any status.
solution: SELECT c.name, COUNT(*) FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id GROUP BY c.id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2

title: Revenue by category
prompt: Total revenue (price times quantity) per product category, counting delivered orders only. Round to 2 decimals and sort highest first.
solution: SELECT p.category, ROUND(SUM(p.price * oi.quantity), 2) AS revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id WHERE o.status = 'delivered' GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY revenue DESC

title: Top three spenders
prompt: Return the names and total spend (delivered orders only, rounded to 2 decimals) of the three customers who spent the most, highest first.
solution: WITH spend AS (SELECT o.customer_id, SUM(p.price * oi.quantity) AS total FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id WHERE o.status = 'delivered' GROUP BY o.customer_id) SELECT c.name, ROUND(s.total, 2) FROM spend s JOIN customers c ON c.id = s.customer_id ORDER BY s.total DESC LIMIT 3

title: Days to first order
prompt: For customers who have ordered, return their name and the whole number of days between signing up and their first order (any status). Fewest days first, then by name.
solution: SELECT c.name, CAST(julianday(MIN(o.ordered_on)) - julianday(c.joined_on) AS INTEGER) AS days FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id GROUP BY c.id ORDER BY days, c.name

title: Daily active users
prompt: For each date with logins, return the date and the number of distinct users who logged in, in date order.
solution: SELECT login_date, COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) FROM logins GROUP BY login_date ORDER BY login_date

title: Next-day retention
prompt: What share of users logged in on the day after they signed up? Return one value between 0 and 1, rounded to 2 decimals.
solution: SELECT ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM logins l WHERE l.user_id = u.id AND l.login_date = date(u.signed_up_on, '+1 day')) THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END), 2) FROM users u

title: Three days in a row
prompt: List the names of users who logged in on at least three consecutive days.
solution: WITH g AS (SELECT user_id, julianday(login_date) - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY login_date) AS island FROM logins), runs AS (SELECT user_id FROM g GROUP BY user_id, island HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3) SELECT DISTINCT u.name FROM runs r JOIN users u ON u.id = r.user_id
